seed_commits.message:
chore: initial service scaffold

FastAPI project, Docker setup and a CI skeleton. No scoring yet.
seed_commits.author: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(model): add the scorer

Hand-written logistic regression over a coefficient artifact rather than a
pickled estimator: reproducible across platforms, reviewable in a diff, and it
keeps the model registry off the code-execution path.
seed_commits.author: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(features): add the spec-driven feature pipeline

Every scale, default and category list comes from the artifact, so a change to
how a feature is computed is a versioned data change rather than a quiet code
edit that diverges from training.
seed_commits.author: Solveig Lindqvist <solveig.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(model): add the artifact registry with compatibility checks

Refuses to serve a model whose feature_spec_version does not match the loaded
spec. Serving a model against the wrong feature contract produces confident
nonsense and is the easiest way to break this service invisibly.
seed_commits.author: Solveig Lindqvist <solveig.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message: feat(artifacts): ship churn_risk v3.0.1 against feature spec 2.1
seed_commits.author: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(api): add predict, batch predict and split health probes

readyz is distinct from healthz on purpose: a container whose artifacts failed
to load must not be reported healthy.
seed_commits.author: Aoife Byrne <aoife.byrne@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(eval): add metrics and the evaluation runner

F1 leads rather than accuracy: the held-out set is 17% positive, so always
predicting 'no churn' scores 83%. The majority baseline is printed next to
accuracy so the comparison cannot be missed.
seed_commits.author: Aoife Byrne <aoife.byrne@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: add the held-out labelled evaluation set

400 accounts. Tenure correlates with plan, as it does in reality, and label
noise is asymmetric -- symmetric noise on an imbalanced set annihilates recall
and makes any F1 bar meaningless.
seed_commits.author: Solveig Lindqvist <solveig.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: cover the scorer, the pipeline and the API contract

Scores are hand-computed against the shipped artifact. The contract suite cares
as much about the 422s as the happy path.
seed_commits.author: Rahul Menon <rahul.menon@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
perf: add a scoring benchmark

Reports operation counts, not just timings. Wall-clock on a loaded laptop varies
severalfold; artifact loads per batch does not.
seed_commits.author: Aoife Byrne <aoife.byrne@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
ci: run tests, the contract suite, the evaluation and the benchmark

ci/run_ci.sh mirrors the workflow so the same steps run locally.
seed_commits.author: Solveig Lindqvist <solveig.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
chore(artifacts): archive every deployed feature-spec version

A prediction stored six months ago is untraceable unless the feature contract
it was made under still exists somewhere. The service does not read this
directory -- it is a record, not a second source of truth -- and nothing yet
compares the active spec against the archived copy of the version it claims to
be. Noted in the README there rather than left for someone to discover.
seed_commits.author: Solveig Lindqvist <solveig.lindqvist@example.com>

seed_commits.message: docs: document the train/serve-skew rules and why F1 leads
seed_commits.author: Aoife Byrne <aoife.byrne@example.com>
